text:
mike: Heads-up — we've seen a sharp uptick in ECC/Xid events on a small subset of cards in us-west-2 this week. Dumping notes here before the oncall runbook call.

anya: ugh. numbers?

mike: Quick paste from the alert aggregation (rolling 7d):
```
- hosts affected: 12 (out of 620 active GPU hosts)
- raw ECC events: 93
- Xid 43/31 spikes correlated to same hosts: ~18 incidents
- estimated GPU-hours impacted: ~2.4k
- noisy cards (~3 hosts) show repeated soft errors, restart doesn't clear
```

katie: That cluster is 80% P4d and 20% A10G last I checked. Are the noisy ones all the same SKU?

mike: Two P4d hosts, one A10G. Mixed. Vendor telemetry shows rising correctable ECC count on the two P4d cards before softlock.

rafa: From spare pool perspective, what's our current safety buffer for us-west-2? I thought we were at 6% spare capacity on reserved fleets.

mike: Yes 6% on dedicated pools. For hosted pools autoscale buys from burst capacity but region-specific limits block us sometimes.

anya: We need to decide: immediate mitigations (drain/replace) vs adjust spare sizing. Also consider RMAs and lead time — vendor says 10-14 business days for replacements to arrive in that region.

katie: Can we quantify impact on capacity if we drain the 12 hosts? If each host has 8 GPUs, that's 96 GPUs. Our active total in us-west-2 is ~7.5k GPUs, so ~1.3% raw. But cluster packing and model shards mean affected SKUs reduce available slots more than 1.3%.

mike: Agreed. My quick sim (very coarse):
```
- baseline failure rate observed (last 12mo, region): 0.9% of GPUs/year
- this week's cluster spike would translate to ~1.6% annualized if sustained
- to keep 99.95% request-availability SLO during rolling drain, we need ~2.8% spare buffer
```

rafa: So number-wise: if we bump from 6% -> 9% spare on dedicated it's an extra ~225 GPUs reserved (costy) but would let us drain/replace without hitting user throttles during mid-sized incidents.

anya: Cost trade-off: reserved capacity has fixed monthly cost; spare uses GPU-hours even idle. For hosted pools we rely on burst allotment but that can be exhausted during cross-region events. Any cheaper alternative? smarter routing to other regions when us-west-2 degrades?

katie: Cross-region routing helps but increases tail latency for some customers and complicates data-sovereignty for enterprise tenants pinned to the region. Not a universal fix.

mike: Suggestion: short-term actions: 1) isolate and drain the 3 repeatedly noisy hosts ASAP (drain + schedule RMA). 2) increase spare pool from 6% -> 8% on dedicated in us-west-2 for 30 days to cover RMA lead time. 3) enable aggressive cache warmers before routing to alternative regions to reduce client-visible latencies.

rafa: I ran a cost delta: moving 2% of capacity into reserved spares (monthly) is ~+$18k/mo for that region. One-off RMA logistics ~$4k. vs potential lost revenue if we had to throttle ~>$120k/mo in worst-case. Numbers look reasonable.

anya: Can we automate detection -> preemptive drain policy for cards that exceed X ECC events threshold within 72h? Current alerting is manual triage.

mike: We have a prototype rule in eng-monitoring: if correctable ECC > 50 in 72h OR Xid 43 count > 3 we flag host for `soft-drain` which stops new allocations and schedules a telemetry snapshot. Want to push to prod but need a rollback plan.

katie: Let's be careful with thresholds to avoid unnecessarily draining transient noise. Maybe require both ECC threshold AND observed process restarts or kernel oops. Add a cool-off window.

mike: Agreed. Proposed policy:
```
- conditions (all): ECC_correctable_72h >= 50 OR Xid_43_count >= 3
- AND either host_restarts_72h >= 1 OR gpu_util_drop_pattern = true
- action: auto soft-drain + tagged for RMA review by SRE team
- metrics emitted: drain_time, RMA_status, replacement_arrival_eta
```

rafa: That looks fine. Operational ask: can eng-infra spin up the +2% reserved spares change and a temporary billing spike approval? I'll need a budget OK from finance for the next 30 days.

anya: I'll ping finance and legal (for enterprise routing constraints). mike/rafa coordinate on the exact host list to drain.

srebot: Incident created: INC-2026-3847, assigned to eng-infra oncall.

mike: I'll start the drain runbook now for the 3 noisy hosts. Putting a note here once complete.

katie: Also let's capture postmortem candidate: are we seeing age-related increase (cards from early 2022 batches)? If yes, we should update the fleet replacement forecasting model (incorporate SKU + manufacture batch) and bake a spare policy per SKU.

mike: noted — I'll export per-SKU failure trajectories and share in the drive.

anya: OK. Agreed temporary +2% spare, auto-drain rule prototype, and full RMA for noisy hosts. Follow-ups: mike to post host IDs & RMA tickets, rafa to get finance approval, katie to draft threshold fine-tuning and rollback plan.

mike: Host drain started. will update thread when RMA scheduled. :thumbsup:

rafa: thx.

katie: good catch, team.
